primitives.name: Surface Enum Divergence
primitives.verbatim_quote: The repo has TWO surface enums with no in-code bridge: model-router `ClaudeSurface` (studio/journal/calibration-insight/model-court/content/brief) and cost-monitor `ClaudeApiSurface` (BLOG_GENERATION/.../OTHER), and call records are keyed to the latter.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'ClaudeSurface': 'enum ∈ {studio, journal, calibration-insight, model-court, content, brief}', 'ClaudeApiSurface': 'enum ∈ {BLOG_GENERATION, ..., OTHER}'}
primitives.assumptions: No direct mapping exists between two surface enums; data integrity depends on external alignment.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Data misalignment if call records use one enum while UI uses another.

layer2.mapping: Two distinct surface enumerations represent same conceptual domain but lack runtime bridging.
layer2.telemetry: Card rendering and budget table display must maintain separate views due to enum mismatch.

The divergence in surface enums introduces a semantic gap that necessitates explicit separation in presentation layers rather than merging. This design avoids runtime ambiguity but requires careful documentation of data flows. The failure mode of type mismatch leads to silent data loss or mislabeling, whereas rule-order violations may lead to suboptimal model selection. Both issues are mitigated through static analysis and controlled rendering logic.
